To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the system of integral equations can be solved for the time-dependent queue-size distributions and that the dropping function has significant impact on the time-dependent queue size.

the time-dependent distribution of queue sizes conditioned by initial number of packets is found and the numerical results for different dropping functions in some network-mitigated traffic scenarios are obtained.

the time-dependent queue-size distributions conditioned by the number (0,1,...,K) of packets present in system initially can be calculated using the system of linear algebra equations, which are built for the Laplace transforms of those distributions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of a GI=M=1 queueing system with a finite buffer and a queue-size dependent packet loss (dropping) probability, which is a generalisation of the well-known GI=M=1 model.
the queue-size dynamics in the finite GI=M=1 model with AQM-type packet-dropping, which is a generalization of the well-known GI=M/1 queue with finite buffer capacity.
the queue size distribution in the GI=M=1 model with finite buffer capacity, in which an arriving packet may be lost with some probability dependent on the instantaneous queue size.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the time-dependent queue-size probability distribution is very sensitive to the dropping function and the traffic intensity.

in case of a finite buffer capacity and a dropping function dependent on queue size the time-dependent queue-size probability distribution conditioned by the initial number of packets in the buffer is not exponential, and the queue-size distribution in case of a saturated buffer is not a mixture of exponentials.
the queue size distribution in the finite GI=M=1 model with AQM-type dropping is a very complex function of the system parameters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the queue-size distribution conditioned on the number of packets initially present in the system, can be obtained by the solution of a system of algebraic equations for the corresponding Laplace transforms.
we have found the time-dependent solution of the finite buffer GI=M=1 queueing system with AQM-type dropping.
the time-dependent queue size distribution in the system with finite buffer and AQM-type dropping function can be calculated using the embedded Markow chain approach and the linear algebra methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the time-dependent queue-size distributions can be obtained in the finite queue model with AQM-type dropping, even in the case of non-Markovian traffic.
the queue-size distribution in such systems is very sensitive to the dropping function and the system parameters, especially the traffic intensity.
the queue-size distribution is not necessarily a decreasing function of the time.
